```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

This exploratory notebook builds on KEC's original exploration of the groundwater
depth dataset published in Ma et al. (2026) (see `Explore_GW_Depths.Rmd`).

This notebook explains some of the decisions behind `process_groundwater_depth.R` and
`calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity.R`, and validates them against the WSD's own
recorded data. A high-level summary of the paper's methods is included below.

The groundwater depth sensitivity indicator scores every water supply.
Groundwater/spring-sourced supplies get a depth-to-water estimate from an
observed static water level where one can be extracted from the WSD's
free-text `description`/`source_notes` fields, falling back to modeled water
table depth (WTD) from `process_groundwater_depth()` where no observed value
is available. All other (surface water) source types are hardcoded to a
depth-to-water of 0. The resulting depth is then binned into a DRASTIC-style
sensitivity score (`raw_groundwater_depth_bin`).

`well_depth`, recorded in the WSD but sparse, is **not** used as a
depth-to-water source. Earlier versions of this indicator used it (assuming a
10 ft well screen: `well_depth - 10 ft`, clipped at 0), but the comparison
below (`#### Comparison between WSD Well Depth Column and Modeled WTD` and the
scatterplots/histograms that follow) shows wells are routinely drilled much
deeper than either the modeled WTD or the observed static water level for the
same sites — well_depth tells you how deep the well was drilled, not where the
water table actually is. That exploration, plus the bin-distribution
comparison in `# Other Explorations` at the end (which reconstructs the old
well-depth-preferred approach and compares it against WTD-only), are both
kept here as the record of why well_depth was dropped from the indicator,
not as a description of current behavior.

# Overview of the paper's methods

- CONUS-wide 1 arc-second (~30m) random forest model, trained on over 1M well
  observations (1914–2023) from USGS, Fan et al., and Jasechko et al.; 10
  physically-motivated input variables (climate, hydraulic conductivity,
  elevation/slope, distance to streams, soil texture) — no x/y coordinates
- 300 decision trees, median of tree outputs is the WTD estimate; held-out test
  performance: r = 0.79, RMSE = 14.94m, NSE = 0.62 (all-observed-cells: r = 0.96,
  RMSE = 6.72m, NSE = 0.93)
- Elevation is by far the dominant predictor (99.55% permutation importance),
  followed by annual mean temperature (94.63%) and precipitation (52.72%)
- Uncertainty is available from the model (interquartile range of the 300 trees'
  outputs per cell), but isn't in the Zenodo raster we're using — see "Things to
  add later" below
- Regional accuracy varies widely: 18 HUC2 basins ranged r = 0.51–0.88, RMSE =
  6.25–28.55m — a single WTD value's reliability depends a lot on where the site is
  relative to the training data. 

Things to add later:

- Pull in the model's uncertainty layer (`wtd_uncertainty`, interquartile range of
  the 300 RF trees' outputs per cell). It's not in the Zenodo download we're
  using — that's point-estimate only — but it's available as a separate
  variable on the same grid via Princeton/HydroFrame's `hf_hydrodata` platform:
  https://hf-hydrodata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gen_ma_2025.html

# Setup

```{r libraries, include = FALSE}
source("setup.R")
```

# Establish file paths

```{r file_paths}
wtd_raster_path <- here("data", "all", "groundwater_sensitivity",
                        "wtd_mean_estimate_RF_additional_inputs_dummy_drop0LP_1s_CONUS2_m_v_20240813.tif")

wtd_all_sites_path <- here("data", "rapid", "inputs", "groundwater_depth",
                           "wtd_all_sites.csv")

gw_sensitivity_files <- list.files(here("data", "rapid", "outputs"),
                                   pattern = "^groundwater_depth_sensitivity_.*\\.csv$",
                                   full.names = TRUE)

gw_sensitivity_path <- gw_sensitivity_files[length(gw_sensitivity_files)]
```

# Import Data

## Water Supply Database — Groundwater Sources

Load the WSD and filter to groundwater/spring source types (the types the
indicator computes an observed-static/modeled-WTD depth for, rather than
hardcoding to 0). `well_depth` is loaded here only to support the
well-depth-vs-WTD/static comparison below — it is not used by the indicator
itself (see note above).

```{r load_wsd}
wsd <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)

wsd_gw <- wsd %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    grepl("groundwater|spring", source_type)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    well_depth = as.numeric(well_depth),
    well_depth_m = well_depth * 0.3048,
    # Assume a 10 ft well screen, so the water table sits ~10 ft above the
    # bottom of the well; clip at 0 for wells shallower than 10 ft.
    well_depth_screen_m = pmax(0, (well_depth - 10) * 0.3048)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name, source_type, well_depth,
                well_depth_m, well_depth_screen_m, description, gwudi, source_notes)
```

Out of the Water Systems Database's `r nrow(wsd)` potential systems,
`r nrow(wsd_gw)` are confirmed groundwater systems and of those
`r sum(!is.na(wsd_gw$well_depth))` have well depth available.

## Water Supplies' Modeled Water Table Depth

These are the results from running `process_groundwater_depth()` in 
`rapid_data_processing.Rmd`.

`process_groundwater_depth()` extracts modeled water table depth (WTD) at each
water supply point from the CONUS-wide random forest WTD model
(https://ngwa.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/gwat.13362). For those points
that do not overlap with the raster dataset and therefore are NA we assign them
the closest available value within a 50km buffer. If there are no data available
within 50km they are assigned NA. At this point there is no source or system 
type filtering. 

```{r load_wtd}
wtd_all_sites <- read_csv(wtd_all_sites_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Out of the Water Systems Database's `r nrow(wsd)` potential systems,
`r sum(!is.na(wtd_all_sites$wtd_point_m))` overlap with the WTD dataset or are within 50km of an
available modeled WTD estimate. `r sum(is.na(wtd_all_sites$wtd_point_m))` water
sources are not within 50km of a modeled WTD estimate.

## Groundwater Depth Sensitivity Indicator

These are the results from running `calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()` in
`rapid_workflow.Rmd`.

`calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()` scores every water supply. For
groundwater/spring source types, it prefers an observed static water level
(extracted from the WSD's free-text `description`/`source_notes` fields) as
the depth-to-water estimate, falling back to modeled water table depth (WTD)
from `process_groundwater_depth()` where no observed value is available.
`well_depth` is not used (see rationale above). All other source types are
hardcoded to a depth-to-water of 0. A `raw_groundwater_depth_source` column
records which source ("observed_static", "modeled_wtd", or "surface_zero") was
used for each site.

The raw depth is also binned into a DRASTIC-style depth-to-water sensitivity
score, using thresholds of 1.5/4.5/9.1/15.2/22.9/30.5 m (5/15/30/50/75/100 ft)
mapped to scores of 1/.9/.7/.5/.3/.2/.1. A shallower water table means higher
sensitivity, so `invert = TRUE` is used when standardizing the raw (continuous)
depth; the bin score is not inverted. A depth of 0 (surface water) naturally
falls into the top bin (1).

```{r load_indicator}
gw_sensitivity <- read_csv(gw_sensitivity_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Out of the Water Systems Database's `r nrow(wsd)` potential systems, all
`r nrow(gw_sensitivity)` have a computed sensitivity score.
`r sum(gw_sensitivity$raw_groundwater_depth_source == "observed_static")` used
an observed static water level, `r sum(gw_sensitivity$raw_groundwater_depth_source == "modeled_wtd")`
fell back to the modeled WTD, and `r sum(gw_sensitivity$raw_groundwater_depth_source == "surface_zero")`
are non-groundwater/spring sources hardcoded to a depth of 0.

## Join the WSD to the processing and indicator calculation results

`gw_all` includes every water supply, not just groundwater-sourced ones, so
that non-groundwater sources show up on maps as `NA` for this indicator
(rather than being silently dropped).

```{r join_all}
gw_all <- wsd %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    well_depth = as.numeric(well_depth),
    well_depth_m = well_depth * 0.3048,
    # Assume a 10 ft well screen, so the water table sits ~10 ft above the
    # bottom of the well; clip at 0 for wells shallower than 10 ft.
    well_depth_screen_m = pmax(0, (well_depth - 10) * 0.3048)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name, source_type, well_depth,
                well_depth_m, well_depth_screen_m, description, gwudi, source_notes) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    wtd_all_sites %>% dplyr::select(wsd_source_id, wtd_point_m),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    gw_sensitivity %>% dplyr::select(-park_unit, -park_name),
    by = "wsd_source_id"
  )
```

# Exploration

## Processing results

### Maps

#### Direct Raster Overlap

Here is an example of a water source site that overlaps with the raster. Note that
the replacement of the the WTD data with the well depth data does not happen 
in the processing script. 

```{r}
site <- wsd %>%
  filter(wsd_source_id == "AGFO_WS_002_01")

wtd <- terra::rast(wtd_raster_path)

site_native <- site %>%
  sf::st_transform(terra::crs(wtd, proj = TRUE))

site_buffer <- site_native %>%
  sf::st_buffer(dist = 5000)

wtd_crop <- terra::crop(wtd, terra::vect(site_buffer))

mapview(wtd_crop, layer.name = "Modeled WTD (m)") +
  mapview(site_native, col.regions = "red", layer.name = "AGFO_WS_002_01")
```

#### Filled via Nearest Valid Cell Within Buffer

Here is an example of a water source the does not overlap with the raster, but
is assigned a value based on the closest available data.

```{r}
site <- wsd %>%
  filter(wsd_source_id == "ACAD_WS_002_01")

wtd <- terra::rast(wtd_raster_path)

site_native <- site %>%
  sf::st_transform(terra::crs(wtd, proj = TRUE))

site_buffer <- site_native %>%
  sf::st_buffer(dist = 50000)

wtd_crop <- terra::crop(wtd, terra::vect(site_buffer))

mapview(wtd_crop, layer.name = "Modeled WTD (m)", maxBytes = 8 * 1024 * 1024) +
  mapview(site_native, col.regions = "red", layer.name = "ACAD_WS_002_01")
```

#### No Valid Cell Found Within Buffer

Based on the current data files, every groundwater/spring-sourced water
supply does have a modeled WTD value (either direct raster overlap or a
nearest-valid-cell fallback); the only sites lacking one are non-groundwater
systems (rainwater catchments on Dry Tortugas, lake-fed systems on Isle
Royale), which the indicator now scores with a hardcoded depth of 0 rather
than a modeled WTD. These are the only sites in the full WSD with no modeled
WTD value within the 50km search buffer:

```{r na_wtd_sites}
missing_depths <- gw_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.na(wtd_point_m))

missing_depths %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, park_name, source_type)
```

```{r na_wtd_map}
mapview(missing_depths, zcol = "source_type", layer.name = "Source Type")
```

```{r na_wtd_table}
missing_depths %>%
  dplyr::select(park_name, park_unit, description, gwudi, source_type, well_depth) %>%
```

#### How Far Is the Nearest-Valid-Cell Fallback Actually Reaching?

`process_groundwater_depth()` fills sites with no direct raster overlap using
the nearest valid cell within a growing search buffer (500m start, doubling,
50km max), but only returns the filled value — not how far away that cell
was. 

This section is added to answer a question from the review:
"Besides Dry Tortugas and Isle Royale (the two sites
that don't get filled even at 50km), how far away were the fallback-filled
sites?" 

```{r fallback_distance_setup}
wtd_fallback <- terra::rast(wtd_raster_path)

points_native <- wsd %>%
  sf::st_transform(terra::crs(wtd_fallback, proj = TRUE))
pts_vect <- terra::vect(points_native)

direct_extract <- terra::extract(wtd_fallback, pts_vect)[, 2]
na_idx <- which(is.na(direct_extract))

start_buffer_m <- 500
max_buffer_m <- 50000
xy_native <- terra::geom(pts_vect)[, c("x", "y")]
wtd_crs <- terra::crs(wtd_fallback)

nearest_valid_distance <- function(i, wtd_path_worker, xy_worker, wtd_crs_worker,
                                    start_buffer_m_worker, max_buffer_m_worker) {
  # Each parallel worker is a separate process, so the raster's underlying
  # pointer has to be re-opened here rather than shared (same reason
  # process_groundwater_depth.R's fill_nearest_valid() does this). This
  # mirrors that function's corrected logic exactly (see its comments for
  # why the two checks below exist) so the distances reported here match
  # what production actually does.
  wtd_worker <- terra::rast(wtd_path_worker)
  pt_vect <- terra::vect(matrix(xy_worker[i, ], nrow = 1), type = "points", crs = wtd_crs_worker)
  buffer_m <- start_buffer_m_worker
  repeat {
    # mask() to the circular buffer, not just crop()'s rectangular bounding
    # box, so a corner cell up to buffer_m * sqrt(2) away can't be picked
    pt_buf <- terra::buffer(pt_vect, width = buffer_m)
    pt_crop <- terra::crop(wtd_worker, pt_buf)
    pt_mask <- terra::mask(pt_crop, pt_buf)
    valid_pts <- terra::as.points(pt_mask, values = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (length(valid_pts) > 0) {
      return(terra::nearest(pt_vect, valid_pts)$distance)
    }
    if (buffer_m >= max_buffer_m_worker) return(NA_real_)
    buffer_m <- min(buffer_m * 2, max_buffer_m_worker)
  }
}

n_workers <- max(1, future::availableCores() - 2)
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = n_workers)
fallback_dist_vals <- furrr::future_map_dbl(
  na_idx, nearest_valid_distance,
  wtd_path_worker = wtd_raster_path, xy_worker = xy_native, wtd_crs_worker = wtd_crs,
  start_buffer_m_worker = start_buffer_m, max_buffer_m_worker = max_buffer_m
)
future::plan(future::sequential)

fallback_distances <- wsd %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::slice(na_idx) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dist_to_valid_cell_m = fallback_dist_vals)
```

```{r fallback_distance_summary}
fallback_reachable <- fallback_distances %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(dist_to_valid_cell_m))

mean_dist_km <- mean(fallback_reachable$dist_to_valid_cell_m) / 1000
median_dist_km <- median(fallback_reachable$dist_to_valid_cell_m) / 1000
max_dist_km <- max(fallback_reachable$dist_to_valid_cell_m) / 1000
```

`r nrow(fallback_distances)` sites had no direct raster overlap;
`r nrow(fallback_reachable)` of those were eventually filled by the growing
search (the remaining `r sum(is.na(fallback_distances$dist_to_valid_cell_m))`
are Dry Tortugas/Isle Royale, shown above). For the filled sites: mean =
`r sprintf("%.2f", mean_dist_km)` km, median = `r sprintf("%.2f", median_dist_km)`
km, max = `r sprintf("%.2f", max_dist_km)` km — max should now be ≤ 50km;
see below.

```{r fallback_distance_hist}
fallback_reachable %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = dist_to_valid_cell_m / 1000)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_dist_km, linetype = "dotted", color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_dist_km, linetype = "dotted", color = "purple") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Distance to Nearest Valid Cell (km)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Fallback-Fill Distance for Sites with No Direct Raster Overlap",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "n = %d; Mean = %.2f km (blue), Median = %.2f km (purple), Max = %.2f km",
      nrow(fallback_reachable), mean_dist_km, median_dist_km, max_dist_km
    )
  )
```

```{r fallback_distance_map}
fallback_reachable_sf <- wsd %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id) %>%
  dplyr::inner_join(fallback_reachable, by = "wsd_source_id")

mapview(fallback_reachable_sf, zcol = "dist_to_valid_cell_m",
        layer.name = "Fallback Distance (m)")
```

```{r fallback_distance_farthest}
fallback_reachable %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(dist_to_valid_cell_m)) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dist_km = round(dist_to_valid_cell_m / 1000, 1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id, park_unit, source_type, dist_km)
```

The farthest fallback-filled sites were mostly Isle Royale (ISRO) — its
Lake Superior island location puts it far from any land-based modeled water
table cell — with Channel Islands (CHIS) as the next-farthest cluster,
offshore from mainland raster coverage.

**This section originally surfaced a real bug**, since fixed in both
`process_groundwater_depth()` and the reconstruction above: distances up to
~81km were coming back despite the documented 50km cap. Two compounding
causes, both now fixed:

1. The growing-buffer loop only checked whether the *current* (pre-doubling)
   buffer radius had reached the cap before trying one more doubled attempt,
   so a check at 32km (still under 50km) still permitted a final try at
   64km. Fixed by clamping the doubled radius to `max_buffer_m` so the last
   attempt lands exactly at the cap.
2. `terra::crop()` only restricts to a buffer's rectangular bounding box,
   not the circular buffer itself, so a valid cell could be accepted from a
   box corner up to `buffer_m * sqrt(2)` away — for a 64km buffer, up to
   ~90.5km, consistent with the ~81km values originally seen here. Fixed by
   `terra::mask()`-ing to the circular buffer polygon before searching, so
   only cells genuinely within the search radius are ever considered.

The numbers above (mean/median/max, histogram, map, farthest-sites table)
reflect this fix — the true max should now be ≤ 50km. If `wtd_all_sites.csv`
was generated before this fix, re-run `process_groundwater_depth()` to
regenerate it with the corrected fallback logic. This makes me want to double
check the other buffer logic in the SLR indicators...

#### Comparison between WSD Well Depth Column and Modeled WTD

Here we display the results from the processing script to the information that is
already in the WSD.

```{r wsd_wtd_comparison}
leafsync::sync(
  mapview(gw_all, zcol = "well_depth_m", layer.name = "WSD Well Depth (m)"),
  mapview(gw_all, zcol = "wtd_point_m", layer.name = "Modeled WTD (m)")
)
```

The well depths are much deeper than the modeled WTD depths, lets look at these
anomalies in the next section.

### Figures

Figures below are restricted to groundwater/spring sources — the source types
the indicator computes an observed-static/modeled-WTD depth for — via
`gw_only` (regardless of `well_depth` availability) and `gw_depth`
(restricted further to sites with a recorded `well_depth`, used only for the
well-depth-vs-WTD/static comparison), rather than the full `gw_all`.

```{r gw_depth_setup}
gw_only <- gw_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("groundwater|spring", source_type))

gw_depth <- gw_only %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(well_depth))

# Formats a p-value for scatterplot subtitles: below 0.001 is reported as
# "< 0.001" rather than rounding down to 0.000
fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.3f", p)

# Wraps long subtitle/title strings so they break onto multiple lines
# instead of overflowing the plot panel (an issue for patchwork-combined
# plots, where each panel only gets half the figure width)
wrap_text <- function(x, width = 80) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = width)
```

#### Scatterplot of the WSD well depths and modeled WTD anomaly

```{r scatter_well_vs_wtd, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
scatter_well_wtd_data <- gw_depth %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(wtd_point_m))

cor_well_wtd <- cor.test(scatter_well_wtd_data$wtd_point_m, scatter_well_wtd_data$well_depth_m)

scatter_well_wtd_data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = wtd_point_m, y = well_depth_m, color = source_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(title.position = "top")) +
  labs(
    x = "Modeled WTD (m)",
    y = "WSD Well Depth (m)",
    color = "Source Type",
    title = "WSD Well Depth vs. Modeled Water Table Depth",
    subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
      "Dashed line = 1:1 agreement; points above the line are wells deeper than the modeled water table. n = %d, Pearson r = %.2f (p %s)",
      nrow(scatter_well_wtd_data), cor_well_wtd$estimate, fmt_p(cor_well_wtd$p.value)
    ), width = 45)
  )
```

#### Distribution of WSD well depth and modeled WTD anomaly

Here we compare well depth to modeled water table depth where both a recorded
well depth and a modeled WTD are available. We compute `well_depth_m - wtd_point_m`
to get a sense of how well the WSD well depth column and the WTD data agree.

A negative gap means the well depth is shallower than the modeled water table,
so the well would not reach the water table if the model were true. These are
sites that indicate that the model is wrong, since we would assume that the well
depths in the WSD are accurate and effective.

A gap smaller than 10m (in either direction) is treated as agreement rather
than a real anomaly — the well and modeled WTD are close enough that the
mismatch is likely measurement/model noise. Only wells more than 10m shallower
than the modeled WTD are flagged as anomalies.

```{r compare_setup}
gap_tolerance_m <- 10

gw_compare <- gw_depth %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(well_depth_m), !is.na(wtd_point_m)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    depth_diff_m = well_depth_m - wtd_point_m,
    depth_diff_flag = dplyr::if_else(
      depth_diff_m < -gap_tolerance_m,
      "Anomaly (well >10m shallower than WTD)",
      "Good (within 10m or well deeper)"
    )
  )
```

```{r compare_hist, fig.height=10}
n_anomaly <- sum(gw_compare$depth_diff_flag == "Anomaly (well >10m shallower than WTD)")
mean_diff <- mean(gw_compare$depth_diff_m)
median_diff <- median(gw_compare$depth_diff_m)

ggplot(gw_compare, aes(x = depth_diff_m, fill = depth_diff_flag)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_diff, linetype = "dotted", color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_diff, linetype = "dotted", color = "purple") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Good (within 10m or well deeper)" = "forestgreen",
    "Anomaly (well >10m shallower than WTD)" = "red"
  )) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title.position = "top")) +
  labs(
    x = "Well Depth − Modeled WTD (m)",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Agreement",
    title = "Gap Between WSD Well Depth and Modeled Water Table Depth",
    subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
      "n = %d sites; %d (%.1f%%) anomalies (>10m shallower). Mean = %.1f m (blue), Median = %.1f m (purple)",
      nrow(gw_compare), n_anomaly, 100 * n_anomaly / nrow(gw_compare), mean_diff, median_diff
    ), width = 85)
  )
```

#### Static Water Level vs. WSD Well Depth

Some `description`/`source_notes` entries state an explicit static water level
(the actual measured depth to water), separate from `well_depth` (how deep the
well was drilled). Here we extract those values using
`extract_static_depth_ft()` (the same helper `calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()`
uses to prioritize observed static levels) and compare them to `well_depth`
for the same sites, to sanity-check the old 10 ft well-screen assumption
(`well_depth - 10 ft`) that used to substitute for this data.

```{r static_setup}
gw_static <- gw_only %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    static_ft = dplyr::coalesce(extract_static_depth_ft(description), extract_static_depth_ft(source_notes)),
    static_m = static_ft * 0.3048
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(static_m))

gw_static_well <- gw_static %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(well_depth_m))

gw_static_wtd <- gw_static %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(wtd_point_m))
```

```{r static_scatter, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
cor_static_well <- cor.test(gw_static_well$static_m, gw_static_well$well_depth_m)

p_static_well <- gw_static_well %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = static_m, y = well_depth_m, color = source_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(title.position = "top")) +
  labs(
    x = "Static Water Level (m)",
    y = "WSD Well Depth (m)",
    color = "Source Type",
    title = "Static Water Level vs. WSD Well Depth",
    subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
      "n = %d sites with an explicit static water level in source_notes/description. Pearson r = %.2f (p %s)",
      nrow(gw_static_well), cor_static_well$estimate, fmt_p(cor_static_well$p.value)
    ), width = 45)
  )

p_static_well
```

#### Validating Extraction Method: Point vs. 4km Buffer Mean

This replicates KEC's original point-vs-buffer-mean validation from
`Explore_GW_Depths.Rmd` (her "Compare results" section), which is what
originally justified `process_groundwater_depth()` using a point extraction
at each water supply's exact coordinates rather than a buffer mean. Her
version ran on a cached n=14 subset; this re-runs the same comparison — same
two extraction methods, same statistics — against the full current ~50-site
static-level set (`gw_static`), for every site with an extracted static level
we compare it to both a raw point extraction and a 4km-buffer mean (with
min/max) from the modeled WTD raster. Point extraction here uses the raw,
non-fallback-filled raster value (`direct_extract`, from the buffer
fallback-distance section above), not `gw_all`'s `wtd_point_m` — mixing in
fallback-filled values would conflate this comparison with the separate
question of how well the nearest-valid-cell fallback performs.

```{r extraction_method_setup}
raw_point_lookup <- wsd %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(wsd_source_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(wtd_point_raw_m = direct_extract)

extraction_compare <- gw_static %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(static_m)) %>%
  sf::st_transform(terra::crs(wtd_fallback, proj = TRUE))

buffer_stats <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(extraction_compare)), function(i) {
  pt <- terra::vect(extraction_compare[i, ])
  pt_buf <- terra::buffer(pt, width = 4000)
  wtd_crop <- terra::crop(wtd_fallback, pt_buf)
  wtd_masked <- terra::mask(wtd_crop, pt_buf)
  tibble::tibble(
    wsd_source_id = extraction_compare$wsd_source_id[i],
    wtd_mean_m = terra::global(wtd_masked, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1],
    wtd_min_m  = terra::global(wtd_masked, "min",  na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1],
    wtd_max_m  = terra::global(wtd_masked, "max",  na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
  )
})

extraction_compare_data <- extraction_compare %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(raw_point_lookup, by = "wsd_source_id") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(buffer_stats, by = "wsd_source_id")
```

```{r extraction_method_stats}
extraction_stats_df <- extraction_compare_data %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(wtd_point_raw_m, wtd_mean_m),
    names_to = "extraction_method",
    values_to = "wtd_modeled_m",
    names_transform = list(extraction_method = ~dplyr::recode(.,
      wtd_point_raw_m = "Point extraction",
      wtd_mean_m      = "4km buffer mean"
    ))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(wtd_modeled_m) & !is.na(static_m)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(extraction_method) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n    = dplyr::n(),
    r    = cor(static_m, wtd_modeled_m, use = "complete.obs"),
    r2   = r^2,
    nse  = 1 - (sum((wtd_modeled_m - static_m)^2) /
           sum((static_m - mean(static_m))^2)),
    rmse = sqrt(mean((wtd_modeled_m - static_m)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    bias = mean(wtd_modeled_m - static_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("n = %d\nr = %.2f\nR² = %.2f\nNSE = %.2f\nRMSE = %.2f m\nBias = %.2f m",
                       n, r, r2, nse, rmse, bias))

extraction_stats_df %>%
  dplyr::select(extraction_method, n, r, r2, nse, rmse, bias)
```

```{r extraction_method_plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
extraction_compare_data %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(wtd_point_raw_m, wtd_mean_m),
    names_to = "extraction_method",
    values_to = "wtd_modeled_m",
    names_transform = list(extraction_method = ~dplyr::recode(.,
      wtd_point_raw_m = "Point extraction",
      wtd_mean_m      = "4km buffer mean"
    ))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = static_m, y = wtd_modeled_m)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "steelblue", fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = ~dplyr::filter(., extraction_method == "4km buffer mean"),
    aes(ymin = wtd_min_m, ymax = wtd_max_m),
    width = 0.5, color = "gray60"
  ) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(
    data = extraction_stats_df,
    aes(label = label),
    x = -Inf, y = Inf,
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
    size = 3.2, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fontface = "plain", family = "mono"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~extraction_method) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x     = "Observed DTW (m)",
    y     = "Modeled DTW (m)",
    title = "Compare National GW Depth Model to NP Water Supply Depths"
  )
```

This confirms KEC's original result (point extraction: r ≈ 0.92, NSE ≈ 0.81,
bias ≈ 0.78m on her n=14 subset) on the larger current sample, and continues
to justify `process_groundwater_depth()`'s use of point extraction over a
buffer mean — see the citation in that function's docstring. I think the buffer mean
underperforms because the modeled WTD surface can change drastically over short
distances, especially near bodies of water.

**Update following review:** the calc function now does use both of these.
`source_type` determines whether a supply gets a groundwater-style depth at
all (groundwater/spring) versus a hardcoded 0 (surface water), since well
depth turned out to be much deeper than the modeled WTD even with the -10ft
adjustment — not a reliable stand-in for water table position regardless of
source type. And the free-text static water level extraction above is now
wired into the calc function as the top-priority depth source, ahead of the
modeled WTD (`extract_static_depth_ft()`, shared with
`calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity.R`) — it was expanded from an earlier,
narrower regex that only matched 39 rows to one that matches 50, still with
no observed false positives on manual spot-check of the previously-unmatched
"static"-containing rows (see git history for the earlier pattern).

## Indicator Calculation Results

This section reflects `calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()`'s actual output
for **all** water supplies (`gw_all`), not just groundwater/spring sources —
surface water types are hardcoded to a depth of 0 (bin 1), so they should show
up here. Earlier sections in this file (well depth, static level, modeled WTD)
were intentionally restricted to `gw_only`/`gw_static` since those are only
meaningful for groundwater/spring sources; this section is different.

### Maps

#### Groundwater Depth Sensitivity — Standardized Bin

Mapping `norm_groundwater_depth_bin`, the standardized (0-1 rescaled) version of
the DRASTIC-style sensitivity score already computed in
`calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()` (thresholds of 1.5/4.5/9.1/15.2/22.9/30.5 m
mapped to scores of 1/.9/.7/.5/.3/.2/.1). The popup shows both the normed bin
and `raw_groundwater_depth_m`, the actual depth value used for the indicator.

```{r sensitivity_bin_map}
m1 <- gw_all %>%
  mapview(
    zcol = "norm_groundwater_depth_bin",
    layer.name = "Groundwater Depth Sensitivity (Bin)",
    popup = leafpop::popupTable(gw_all, zcol = c("norm_groundwater_depth_bin", "raw_groundwater_depth_m"))
  )

m1
```

### Figures

#### Distribution of WTD bins

Count of **all** water supplies in each DRASTIC-style bin score (thresholds
of 1.5/4.5/9.1/15.2/22.9/30.5 m mapped to scores of 1/.9/.7/.5/.3/.2/.1).
Surface water sources (hardcoded to depth 0) should dominate bin 1.

```{r sensitivity_bin_bar}
bin_levels <- c("0.1", "0.2", "0.3", "0.5", "0.7", "0.9", "1")

p1_all <- gw_all %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(raw_groundwater_depth_bin)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(bin_factor = factor(raw_groundwater_depth_bin, levels = bin_levels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bin_factor, fill = bin_factor)) +
  geom_bar(color = "white") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Bin Score (Low Risk → High Risk)",
    y = "Count",
    title = wrap_text("Distribution of Groundwater Depth Sensitivity Bins (All Water Supplies)", width = 45)
  )

p1_all
```

Distribution of `raw_groundwater_depth_m` (the actual depth value used for the
indicator) across all water supplies, with the DRASTIC-style bin thresholds
marked as vlines, capped at 100m to keep a small number of very deep outliers
from flattening the plot. Expect a large spike at 0 from surface water
sources.

```{r sensitivity_bin_hist}
bin_thresholds_m <- c(1.5, 4.5, 9.1, 15.2, 22.9, 30.5)

gw_depth_plot_all <- gw_all %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(raw_groundwater_depth_m))

outlier_cutoff_m <- 100
n_outliers <- sum(gw_depth_plot_all$raw_groundwater_depth_m > outlier_cutoff_m)

gw_depth_plot_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(raw_groundwater_depth_m <= outlier_cutoff_m) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = raw_groundwater_depth_m, fill = factor(raw_groundwater_depth_bin, levels = bin_levels))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = bin_thresholds_m, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Groundwater Depth Used for Indicator (m)",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Bin Score",
    title = "Distribution of Groundwater Depth with DRASTIC Bin Demarcations (All Water Supplies)",
    subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
      "Dashed lines = DRASTIC thresholds (1.5/4.5/9.1/15.2/22.9/30.5 m). %d outlier(s) above %d m excluded.",
      n_outliers, outlier_cutoff_m
    ), width = 85)
  )
```

# Other Explorations

`well_depth` is no longer part of `calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()` (see
the review discussion above), so it isn't in `raw_groundwater_depth_bin`
anymore. This section recreates, purely for demonstration, what the
indicator looked like when it *did* prefer `well_depth` over modeled WTD
(the pre-review approach: `well_depth - 10 ft` screen assumption, falling
back to WTD) and compares it against WTD-only — the same comparison this
section always made, kept here as a record of how weak a signal `well_depth`
actually was, which is part of why it was dropped.

This is computed locally in this section only, from `well_depth_screen_m`
and `wtd_point_m` (both already on `gw_only`) — it does not reflect what
`calc_groundwater_depth_sensitivity()` currently does, and is intentionally
restricted to `gw_only` (groundwater/spring sources), same as always.

```{r other_explorations_setup}
gw_well_depth_pref <- gw_only %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    raw_depth_well_depth_pref = dplyr::coalesce(well_depth_screen_m, wtd_point_m),
    bin_well_depth_pref = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 0, 1.5)     ~ 1,
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 1.5, 4.5)   ~ .9,
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 4.5, 9.1)   ~ .7,
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 9.1, 15.2)  ~ .5,
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 15.2, 22.9) ~ .3,
      dplyr::between(raw_depth_well_depth_pref, 22.9, 30.5) ~ .2,
      raw_depth_well_depth_pref >= 30.5                     ~ .1,
      .default = NA
    ),
    bin_well_depth_pref_norm = scales::rescale(bin_well_depth_pref, to = c(0, 1))
  )

p1_gw <- gw_well_depth_pref %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(bin_well_depth_pref)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(bin_factor = factor(bin_well_depth_pref, levels = bin_levels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bin_factor, fill = bin_factor)) +
  geom_bar(color = "white") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Bin Score (Low Risk → High Risk)",
    y = "Count",
    title = wrap_text("Distribution of Groundwater Depth Sensitivity Bins (Well Depth Preferred)", width = 45)
  )
```

```{r wtd_only_bin_setup}
gw_wtd_only <- gw_only %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(wtd_point_m)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    wtd_bin = dplyr::case_when(
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 0, 1.5)     ~ 1,
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 1.5, 4.5)   ~ .9,
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 4.5, 9.1)   ~ .7,
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 9.1, 15.2)  ~ .5,
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 15.2, 22.9) ~ .3,
      dplyr::between(wtd_point_m, 22.9, 30.5) ~ .2,
      wtd_point_m >= 30.5                     ~ .1,
      .default = NA
    ),
    wtd_bin_norm = scales::rescale(wtd_bin, to = c(0, 1))
  )
```

```{r wtd_only_bin_hist}
outlier_cutoff_wtd_m <- 100
n_outliers_wtd <- sum(gw_wtd_only$wtd_point_m > outlier_cutoff_wtd_m)

gw_wtd_only %>%
  dplyr::filter(wtd_point_m <= outlier_cutoff_wtd_m) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = wtd_point_m, fill = factor(wtd_bin, levels = bin_levels))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = bin_thresholds_m, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Modeled WTD (m)",
    y = "Count",
    fill = "Bin Score",
    title = wrap_text("Distribution of Modeled WTD with DRASTIC Bin Demarcations (WTD Only)", width = 70),
    subtitle = wrap_text(sprintf(
      "Dashed lines = DRASTIC thresholds (1.5/4.5/9.1/15.2/22.9/30.5 m). %d outlier(s) above %d m excluded.",
      n_outliers_wtd, outlier_cutoff_wtd_m
    ), width = 85)
  )
```

#### Difference in bin distribution between well-depth-preferred and WTD-only

Comparing the count of sites in each bin under the well-depth-preferred
reconstruction (`bin_well_depth_pref`) against the WTD-only method
(`wtd_bin`). Positive bars mean the WTD-only method puts more sites in that
bin than well-depth-preferred; negative bars mean fewer.

```{r bin_diff_setup}
current_counts <- gw_well_depth_pref %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(bin_well_depth_pref)) %>%
  dplyr::count(bin_factor = factor(bin_well_depth_pref, levels = bin_levels), name = "n_current")

wtd_only_counts <- gw_wtd_only %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::count(bin_factor = factor(wtd_bin, levels = bin_levels), name = "n_wtd_only")

bin_diff <- dplyr::full_join(current_counts, wtd_only_counts, by = "bin_factor") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_current = tidyr::replace_na(n_current, 0),
    n_wtd_only = tidyr::replace_na(n_wtd_only, 0),
    diff = n_wtd_only - n_current
  )
```

```{r bin_diff_bar}
bin_diff %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = bin_factor, y = diff, fill = diff > 0)) +
  geom_col(color = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "forestgreen"), guide = "none") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Bin Score (Low Risk → High Risk)",
    y = "Difference in Count (WTD Only − Well Depth Preferred)",
    title = wrap_text("Difference in Bin Distribution: WTD-Only vs. Well-Depth-Preferred", width = 70),
    subtitle = "Red = more sites in that bin under WTD-only; Green = fewer"
  )
```
